security.title: Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass
security.description:
[CVE-2024-0056](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-98g6-xh36-x2p7): Microsoft.Data.SqlClient and System.Data.SqlClient vulnerable to SQL Data Provider Security Feature Bypass 

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range < 2.1.7; first patched 2.1.7)
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range >= 3.0.0, < 3.1.5; first patched 3.1.5)
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range >= 4.0.0, < 4.0.5; first patched 4.0.5)
  - Microsoft.Data.SqlClient 2.1.4 (packages.config:14; affected range >= 5.0.0, < 5.1.3; first patched 5.1.3)

Recommended fix: Upgrade the affected package to a version outside its vulnerable range.

security.title: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
security.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: NotificationService creates the private message queue and grants the Everyone principal MessageQueueAccessRights.FullControl at line 23, allowing unintended local actors to read, send, and modify queue messages.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: BaseController.SendEntityNotification records create/update/delete events with the hard-coded actor name "System" (lines 24-29), despite the operations being initiated by users; the audit event therefore omits the responsible identity.

security.title: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Edit binds TeachingMaterialImagePath from the request (line 130), then maps it with Server.MapPath and deletes the resulting file (lines 170-175) without confirming it remains under the teaching-material upload directory.

security.title: Relative Path Traversal
security.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Edit accepts TeachingMaterialImagePath from the request and passes it to Server.MapPath before deleting the resulting path (lines 130, 170-175); relative traversal segments are not rejected or constrained to the upload directory.

security.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
security.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Create and Edit validate only the client-supplied filename extension against an image-extension allowlist (lines 55-58 and 138-141), then save the uninspected request bytes under the web-accessible Uploads directory (lines 76-88 and 159-181). The content is not verified to be an image, so non-image content can be stored with an allowed image extension.

security.title: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
security.description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.

evidence.explanation: CoursesController.Edit accepts TeachingMaterialImagePath from request binding and uses it as a filesystem resource identifier via Server.MapPath before deleting the file (lines 130, 170-175).

security.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
security.description: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.

evidence.explanation: NotificationService.ReceiveNotification reads the message body from the message queue and deserializes it into Notification with JsonConvert.DeserializeObject at line 76, without validating the resulting object. The queue is configured with Everyone FullControl at lines 20-23, so the body is not inherently trusted.
